quests.instruction: Which animal can waddle calmly, but can act fast to stay safe?
quests.hint: This animal lives wandering through the forest at night.
quests.explanation: Yes! The skunk can waddle calmly, but can act fast to stay safe. It has a black coat with a white stripe.
quests.funFact: A skunk's spray is so strong it can be smelled over a mile away.

quests.instruction: Who is able to climb trees and tumble playfully? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives munching bamboo in a misty forest.
quests.explanation: Yes! The panda can climb trees and tumble playfully. It has round black and white patches.
quests.funFact: Did you know? pandas spend almost their entire day just eating bamboo.

quests.instruction: This animal says "Snort"! Which one is it?
quests.hint: Think of an animal that lives grazing on the open plains.
quests.explanation: Yes! A rhino says "Snort". It also has one or two horns and very thick skin.
quests.funFact: Did you know? rhinos have terrible eyesight but incredible hearing and smell.

quests.instruction: What do we call a group of alpacas?
quests.hint: Think about where alpacas usually live: grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.explanation: Yes! A group of alpacas is called a herd. They like to stay together grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.funFact: Elephants have a matriarchal herd, led by the oldest and wisest female.

quests.instruction: Listen closely! Who says "Tap-tap-tap"?
quests.hint: Think of an animal that lives pecking at a tall forest tree.
quests.explanation: Yes! A woodpecker says "Tap-tap-tap". It also has a strong pointed beak and stiff tail feathers.
quests.funFact: Woodpeckers have special shock-absorbing skulls so they don't get headaches from pecking.

quests.instruction: Who is able to sprint faster than any other land animal? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives sprinting across the open plains.
quests.explanation: Yes! The cheetah can sprint faster than any other land animal. It has a slim body with black spots built for speed.
quests.funFact: Cheetahs cannot roar; instead, they purr just like house cats.

quests.instruction: I have long legs and the biggest eyes of any land animal. I live running across the open plains. I can run very fast instead of flying. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a bird.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the ostrich! It has long legs and the biggest eyes of any land animal and lives running across the open plains.
quests.funFact: Did you know? they are the fastest running birds on Earth.

quests.instruction: Which animal's baby is called a "cria"?
quests.hint: The grown-up animal lives grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.explanation: Correct! A baby alpaca is called a cria. The alpaca has a long neck and a soft woolly coat.
quests.funFact: Alpacas hum to communicate with each other.

quests.instruction: Which animal can climb and use clever paws like tiny hands?
quests.hint: This animal lives exploring the forest at night.
quests.explanation: Yes! The raccoon can climb and use clever paws like tiny hands. It has a black mask around the eyes and clever paws.
quests.funFact: They are highly adaptable and incredibly clever problem solvers.

quests.instruction: A baby blue whale has a special name. What is it called?
quests.hint: Baby animal names are often short and sweet, just like an enormous body and a giant heart.
quests.explanation: That's it! A baby blue whale is called a calf. Grown-up blue whales live gliding through the deep ocean.
quests.funFact: Did you know? a baby cow or elephant is called a calf.

quests.instruction: A baby koala has a special name. What is it called?
quests.hint: Baby animal names are often short and sweet, just like round fuzzy ears and a big black nose.
quests.explanation: That's it! A baby koala is called a joey. Grown-up koalas live resting in a eucalyptus tree in Australia.
quests.funFact: A joey is the size of a jellybean when it is first born.

quests.instruction: One of these animals lives in a garden. Which one?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with dry, bumpy skin.
quests.explanation: Great job! The toad lives in a garden. You can spot it by dry, bumpy skin.
quests.funFact: Did you know? they secrete a bitter toxin from their skin to deter predators.

quests.instruction: Can you spot the animal with a long neck and a soft woolly coat?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.explanation: That's right! The alpaca has a long neck and a soft woolly coat. You can find it grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.funFact: Alpaca fleece is softer and warmer than sheep's wool.

quests.instruction: I have large digging paws and tiny eyes. I live digging tunnels underground. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a mammal.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the mole! It has large digging paws and tiny eyes and lives digging tunnels underground.
quests.funFact: Moles have extra thumbs to help them dig tunnels faster.

quests.instruction: I have wide wings and the ability to sleep upside down. I live flying through the night sky. I can fly at night. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a mammal.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the bat! It has wide wings and the ability to sleep upside down and lives flying through the night sky.
quests.funFact: Did you know? bats are the only mammals capable of sustained flight.

quests.instruction: Which animal has a slim body with black spots built for speed?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives sprinting across the open plains.
quests.explanation: That's right! The cheetah has a slim body with black spots built for speed. You can find it sprinting across the open plains.
quests.funFact: Their non-retractable claws give them extra grip when running fast.

quests.instruction: I have a long neck and a soft woolly coat. I live grazing on a mountain farm. I can walk calmly and hum softly. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a mammal.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the alpaca! It has a long neck and a soft woolly coat and lives grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.funFact: Alpacas are very social and love being in herds.

quests.instruction: Can you spot the animal with smooth flippers and big round eyes?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives resting on icy Arctic rocks.
quests.explanation: That's right! The seal has smooth flippers and big round eyes. You can find it resting on icy Arctic rocks.
quests.funFact: They can sleep underwater, occasionally bobbing up for air automatically.

quests.instruction: What do we call a group of seals?
quests.hint: Think about where seals usually live: resting on icy Arctic rocks.
quests.explanation: Yes! A group of seals is called a colony. They like to stay together resting on icy Arctic rocks.
quests.funFact: Emperor penguin colonies huddle together for warmth in the freezing cold.

quests.instruction: Which animal can walk calmly and hum softly?
quests.hint: This animal lives grazing on a mountain farm.
quests.explanation: Yes! The alpaca can walk calmly and hum softly. It has a long neck and a soft woolly coat.
quests.funFact: They use a communal dung pile to keep their grazing area clean.

quests.instruction: Where would you find this animal? Who lives in a garden?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with large digging paws and tiny eyes.
quests.explanation: Great job! The mole lives in a garden. You can spot it by large digging paws and tiny eyes.
quests.funFact: They can dig up to 18 feet of tunnel in just one hour.

quests.instruction: I have a strong pointed beak and stiff tail feathers. I live pecking at a tall forest tree. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a bird.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the woodpecker! It has a strong pointed beak and stiff tail feathers and lives pecking at a tall forest tree.
quests.funFact: Their tongues are so long they wrap around their brains for extra protection.

quests.instruction: Which animal is a bird?
quests.hint: This animal has a big, colorful striped beak.
quests.explanation: Yes! The puffin is a bird. It lives nesting on a cold, rocky cliff.
quests.funFact: Did you know? puffins can hold dozens of small fish in their specialized beaks at once.

quests.instruction: What do we call a group of otters?
quests.hint: Think about where otters usually live: floating belly-up on a calm river.
quests.explanation: Yes! A group of otters is called a raft. They like to stay together floating belly-up on a calm river.
quests.funFact: A group of otters resting on the water is called a raft.

quests.instruction: I have large digging paws and tiny eyes. I live digging tunnels underground. I can dig quickly through soft soil. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a mammal.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the mole! It has large digging paws and tiny eyes and lives digging tunnels underground.
quests.funFact: Moles have tiny eyes and rely mostly on their sense of touch and smell.

quests.instruction: Which animal makes its home in a garden?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with a curly, spiral-shaped shell.
quests.explanation: Great job! The snail lives in a garden. You can spot it by a curly, spiral-shaped shell.
quests.funFact: Did you know? snails can sleep for up to three years if the weather is too dry.

quests.instruction: Who is able to peck rapidly and cling to tree trunks? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives pecking at a tall forest tree.
quests.explanation: Yes! The woodpecker can peck rapidly and cling to tree trunks. It has a strong pointed beak and stiff tail feathers.
quests.funFact: Woodpeckers drum on trees to communicate and claim territory.

quests.instruction: Look carefully! Which animal has eight legs and a silky web?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives weaving a web in the garden.
quests.explanation: That's right! The spider has eight legs and a silky web. You can find it weaving a web in the garden.
quests.funFact: Did you know? most spiders have eight eyes, but some have almost no vision at all.

quests.instruction: A group of ants has a special name. What is it?
quests.hint: Think about where ants usually live: marching through the garden.
quests.explanation: Yes! A group of ants is called a colony. They like to stay together marching through the garden.
quests.funFact: Colonies rely on incredible teamwork to survive.

quests.instruction: What do we call a baby cheetah?
quests.hint: Baby animal names are often short and sweet, just like a slim body with black spots built for speed.
quests.explanation: That's it! A baby cheetah is called a cub. Grown-up cheetahs live sprinting across the open plains.
quests.funFact: Bear cubs are born blind, hairless, and very tiny.
